topic: Schumann 7.83 Hz stable — verification of c10 mechanical fixes (ISS-2929)
change_summary: Verification of decider commit 5141233 (ISS-2929) — four mechanical c10 fixes to detail_evidence: reconciled area-weighted H(r) with WIN-002 (2,140 km / 35 Hz, was 1,800 km / 42 Hz), tightened radial average to 3,316 km / 22.6 Hz (was 3,400 km / 22 Hz), fixed 27 Hz → 28 Hz rounding at r = 10,000 km.
our_argument_summary: The dome's own H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) km places its quarter-wave floor at 8.78 Hz at the pole and rising monotonically outward; 7.83 Hz sits below that floor at every point. The four transverse-mode escapes (parallel-plate quarter-wave, spherical TM, cylindrical Bessel, coupled-eigenvalue) either preserve the pole-floor, import a globe fingerprint, or fail to land at 7.83 Hz from dome geometry alone. Verdict: Self-Contradicted.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard atmospheric physics fully explains the 7.83 Hz Schumann fundamental via Earth's spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity plus D-layer damping (Schumann 1952, Sentman 1987/1990, Nickolaenko & Hayakawa 2002). Dome model relabels this as evidence of a firmament without producing 7.83 Hz from its own geometry.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: The 7.83 Hz Schumann fundamental has been continuously measured since the 1960s and theoretically predicted since 1952 — 74 years prior to the dome model's OTS registration. Registering a 74-year-old measurement is textbook post-hoc.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The dome's own H(r) does NOT produce 7.83 Hz — the pole-floor 8.78 Hz is the minimum achievable frequency from the published H(r), and 7.83 Hz cannot be derived from dome geometry via any published mode formula (quarter-wave, spherical TM, cylindrical Bessel).

holes_found.description: TLDR-vs-detail inconsistency introduced by incomplete ISS-2929 self-apply. The decider commit 5141233 correctly patched detail_evidence 'at r = 10,000 km, f ≈ 27 Hz' → 'f ≈ 28 Hz', but did NOT touch tldr_evidence, which still reads: '…rising monotonically outward (27 Hz at r = 10,000 km, ~90 Hz at the rim).' A reader following progressive-disclosure UX (TLDR before expanding) will see 27 Hz in the summary and 28 Hz in the detail — a visible cross-field arithmetic contradiction in the exact same argument. Per the review rubric's TLDR Review section, factual mismatches between TLDR and expanded content are flagged as major because TLDRs are what most readers see and never expand past. This one is unusually clear because c10 hole #1 explicitly flagged 27 Hz as a rounding error requiring correction (the correct rounding of H(10,000)=2,675.6 km → f=28.01 Hz is 28 Hz), the decider applied the correction to detail but stopped there. Verified by grep on the fresh clone (post git pull --rebase): wins.json tldr_evidence has '27 Hz' = true, has '28 Hz' = false; detail_evidence has the opposite. No other '27 Hz' or '1,800 km' or '42 Hz' strings remain in wins.json — only the TLDR miss.
holes_found.recommendation: One-character patch: in WIN-038.tldr_evidence, replace '27 Hz at r = 10,000 km' with '28 Hz at r = 10,000 km'. No other TLDR content needs adjustment (the 8.78 Hz pole-floor, ~90 Hz rim, and Earth 40,075 km circumference figures are all still correct). Trivial decider self-apply.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model's underlying observation that the Schumann fundamental sits near 7.83 Hz and remains stable is factually correct (Sentman 1987, doi:10.1029/RS022i004p00595). And the intuition that a resonance frequency implies a cavity geometry is scientifically sound — that is precisely how Schumann (1952) originally back-derived Earth's ionospheric cavity. The dome model is doing the same category of reasoning; it just arrives at the wrong cavity (see WIN-038 detail_evidence pole-floor paragraph).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Getting the observation right and using the right category of reasoning does not save WIN-038 because the dome's own H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) km places the achievable quarter-wave frequency floor at 8.78 Hz at the pole and rising monotonically outward (WIN-038 detail_evidence pole-floor paragraph). 7.83 Hz is below that floor at every radius on the disc — no averaging or mode-choice trick can rescue the claim without either (a) importing globe circumference geometry into the disc-cavity mode formula (WIN-038 detail_evidence argument (ii)) or (b) simultaneously withdrawing the WIN-029 back-derivation that inversely uses f = c/(4H) (WIN-038 detail_evidence argument (i)). Being partially right about the observation just makes the geometric contradiction sharper.

deeper_analysis: This c11 is a narrow verification of ISS-2929's four mechanical patches. All four landed in detail_evidence exactly as claimed in the commit message; all four are arithmetically correct; and the cross-WIN consistency with WIN-002 (both averaging figures) and cross-file consistency with sections.json §2.1 supplementary averaging block are now clean. The one hole discovered — the TLDR still saying 27 Hz — is a straightforward miss of scope: the ISS-2929 patch described itself as 'detail_evidence' work, and tldr_evidence is a separate field the decider did not touch. TLDR-hole discipline (rubric section 'TLDR Review (all items)') makes this major, and one-character-patch trivial to fix. All four carry-over c10 holes are already tracked in EXPs (647, 648) per the decider commit message so no new ISS creation is warranted for those. Advocate-mode counter-argument (per curmudgeon-change-and-holistic.md): could a defender claim the TLDR 27 Hz is deliberately a coarser rounding for a lay audience while the detail uses the precise 28 Hz? No — because (a) both the TLDR and the detail cite the same specific radius r = 10,000 km, so precision cannot legitimately differ between summary and detail on a shared anchor point, and (b) the c10 review explicitly flagged 27 Hz as a factual rounding error that had to be fixed, meaning any 'coarse rounding' defense contradicts our own on-record standard. The TLDR fix is required for consistency of standard, not merely aesthetics.
